title: Cycle flex lanes and critical-path pruning
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and operationalize a lightweight 'flex lanes' framework for cycle staffing and scope decisions. The goal is to preserve OKR-facing commitments while creating explicit lanes for discretionary, exploratory, and risk-mitigation work. Deliverables: (1) decision rubric for critical-path pruning when capacity is tight, (2) staffing swap/playbook for short-term reassignments, (3) a one-page cycle runbook for PMs and EMs to apply during weekly checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page runbook published in Drive linked from this ticket
A triage rubric with measurable thresholds (e.g., >=10% velocity erosion triggers level-1 pruning) documented and reviewed by Eng and Design
Staffing swap playbook with at least two tested examples and a nominated backup pool of engineers
Two simulated scenario runs (5% and 20% capacity loss) with concrete scope cut actions and owners
Sign-off from Head of PM and Head of Eng on final runbook
comments: 2025-02-15 Maya Chen: Kickoff — framing the problem: teams are frequently forced into ad-hoc scope cuts mid-cycle which causes churn. Proposed 'flex lanes' (core, buffer, opportunistic) to reduce ad-hoc decisions.

2025-02-17 Ethan Park: Met with Alex (Eng) and Priya (Design) to align. Agreed to test two simulations and validate thresholds against historical cycle data. Assigned simulation owners: Alex -> 5% loss, Priya -> 20% loss.
2025-02-19 Alex Rivera (ENG): Pulled velocity history for last 6 cycles. Noted median mid-cycle velocity drop 8% during high-support weeks. Proposed threshold: >12% = 'level-2' actions.
2025-02-21 Design review (Priya): Suggested rewording of 'opportunistic' lane to 'proof-of-value' lane to reduce interpretation friction with stakeholders. Updated labels accordingly.
2025-02-23 Ethan Park: Draft runbook posted: https://drive.google.com/example-runbook. Shared with PMs for feedback — ask for review by 2025-02-25.
2025-02-25 Sarah Liu (PM): Feedback: add explicit guardrails for customer-impacting work (do not cut bug fixes that are P0/P1). Also request example language for communicating scope cuts to execs.

2025-02-26 Maya Chen: Incorporated Sarah feedback and added two canned communication templates. Updated simulation artifacts and uploaded spreadsheet with scenario math: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheet-simulations
2025-02-27 Ethan Park: Preparing sign-off doc for Head of PM & Head of Eng. Next: tabletop rehearsal with three PM/EM pairs on 2025-03-03.

Incorporate rehearsal notes and finalize runbook by 2025-03-05
